slides.0.title: Level 2 final assessment
slides.0.subtitle: The language of business questions: cost, channel, brand, trend
slides.1.title: Level 2 key points
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Cost and price
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Steep slopes, low yields and long ageing raise costs; fixed duty and packaging mean little wine value in cheap bottles; price is a compromise of cost, competition and perceived value
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Channels and policy
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Retail, on-trade, monopolies and three-tier; Granholm v. Heald (2005); China’s duties on Australian wine (2020 to March 2024); DTC has the highest margins; La Place and en primeur
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Brands and trends
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Brands and appellations are two kinds of trust; side effects of scores; 2025 consumption the lowest since 1961; premiumisation; sustainability claims need certification
slides.1.content: The key to scoring in business essays: every number dated, every point with a mechanism.

Why are steep, hand-worked vineyards more expensive?

A. Cross-regional and multi-vintage blending, plus scale
